bug.title: Deleting a todo while filtered removes the wrong item from the underlying list
observed_steps: 00:04 — User adds 'Pay rent' (all three items are visible in the 'All' view)
00:05 — User marks 'Buy milk' as done (checkbox checked, text struck through)
00:06 — User clicks the 'Active' filter button, showing only 'Walk dog' and 'Pay rent'
00:07 — User clicks the delete ('×') button on 'Walk dog', leaving only 'Pay rent' in the 'Active' view
00:08 — User clicks thedelete ('×') button on 'Pay rent' (or switches back to 'All' at 00:09)
00:09 — User switches to the 'All' filter, revealing that 'Buy milk' (done) and 'Pay rent' are still present, while 'Buy milk' was supposed to be kept or deleted properly
bug.expected: When deleting 'Walk dog' (the first item in the 'Active' filter), 'Walk dog' should be removed from `todos` while 'Buy milk' (completed) and 'Pay rent' remain. Or more generally, clicking delete on a visible item in a filtered view should delete that exact item by its `id`.
bug.actual: In the 'Active' filter at 00:06, 'Walk dog' is at visible index 0 (while 'Buy milk' is at index 0 in the full `todos` array). When the user clicks delete on 'Walk dog', `deleteTodo(0)` splices index 0 of `todos` ('Buy milk'). However, at 00:07 'Walk dog' disappears and 'Pay rent' remains in Active view, and at 00:09 switching to 'All' shows 'Buy milk' (checked) and 'Pay rent' — meaning clicking delete on 'Pay rent' (index 1 in Active view) deleted 'Walk dog' (index 1 in `todos`) instead of 'Pay rent'!
evidence_timestamps: 00:05 — In 'All' filter, 'Buy milk' is checked as done at index 0, 'Walk dog' is at index 1, 'Pay rent' is at index 2.
00:06 — Switched to 'Active' filter: visible items are 'Walk dog' (visible index 0) and 'Pay rent' (visible index 1).
00:07 — User clicks delete on 'Pay rent' (visible index 1 in 'Active' filter), which actually deletes index 1 of `todos` ('Walk dog'), leaving only 'Pay rent' visible in 'Active'.
00:09 — User switches back to 'All' filter: 'Buy milk' (done) and 'Pay rent' are still in the list, proving 'Walk dog' was deleted when the user clicked delete on 'Pay rent'.
bug.root_cause_hypothesis: In `app/public/app.js`, `render()` iterates over `visibleTodos()` with `items.forEach((t, i) => ...)` and binds the delete button click handler to `deleteTodo(i)` (line 88), passing the index `i` within the filtered `items` array rather than the todo's unique `t.id`. `deleteTodo(index)` (lines 47-52) then calls `todos.splice(index, 1)` on the unfiltered `todos` array. When a filter like 'Active' or 'Done' is applied, the index in `visibleTodos()` does not match the index in `todos`, causing the wrong todo item to be removed. `deleteTodo` should accept `id` (like `toggleTodo` does) and remove the matching todo by `t.id`.

verdict.original_video_summary: The user added three todos ('Buy milk', 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent'), marked 'Buy milk' as completed (00:05), and switched to the 'Active' filter (00:06) where 'Walk dog' (visible index 0) and 'Pay rent' (visible index 1) were shown. When deleting an item in the filtered view (00:07), `deleteTodo` spliced the unfiltered `todos` array by the filtered visible index instead of the item's `id`, deleting the wrong todo item.
verdict.fixed_video_summary: The automated test added 'Buy milk', 'Walk dog', and 'Pay rent' (00:01–00:03), marked 'Buy milk' as done (00:04), switched to the 'Active' filter and deleted 'Walk dog' (00:05), leaving only 'Pay rent' in the 'Active' list. Switching back to 'All' (00:06) showed both 'Buy milk' (completed) and 'Pay rent' intact, confirming that deleting 'Walk dog' at visible index 0 in 'Active' removed 'Walk dog' rather than 'Buy milk' (index 0 in `todos`).
verdict.comparison: In the original recording (00:06–00:09), deleting an item while on the 'Active' tab used the filtered array index `i` to splice the main `todos` array, causing a mismatch whenever completed items preceded active items. In the fixed recording, after marking 'Buy milk' (index 0 in `todos`) as done at 00:04, the test switches to 'Active' and deletes 'Walk dog' (visible index 0 in 'Active') at 00:05: 'Walk dog' is immediately removed leaving only 'Pay rent', and switching to 'All' at 00:06 confirms 'Buy milk' was not accidentally spliced from index 0 of `todos`.
verdict.pr_description:
## Context
When viewing a filtered list of todos (`Active` or `Done`), clicking the delete (`×`) button on a todo item removed the wrong item from the underlying `todos` list.

## Root Cause
In `app/public/app.js`, `render()` iterated over `visibleTodos()` and bound each delete button to `deleteTodo(i)` using the item's index `i` in the filtered array. `deleteTodo(index)` then called `todos.splice(index, 1)` on the unfiltered `todos` array.

## Fix
- Updated `deleteTodo(id)` to accept the todo's unique `id` and filter `todos` by `t.id !== id`.
- Updated the delete button click handler in `render()` to call `deleteTodo(t.id)`.

## Verification
Verified via automated Playwright test: created three todos (`Buy milk`, `Walk dog`, `Pay rent`), completed `Buy milk`, switched to the `Active` filter, deleted `Walk dog` (first visible item in `Active`), and verified that `Walk dog` was removed while `Buy milk` and `Pay rent` remained when switching back to `All`.

rationale: In `app/public/app.js`, `render()` passed the filtered list index `i` to `deleteTodo(index)`, which spliced `todos` at `index` rather than removing the target todo by its unique `id`. When viewing a filtered subset ('Active' or 'Done'), the visible index does not match the index in the main `todos` array. Updating `deleteTodo` to accept `id` and filter `todos` by `t.id !== id` (and passing `t.id` from the delete button click handler) ensures the exact item is removed regardless of the active filter.
